header.name: Quentin Lopes
header.subtitle: Game Developer • Unreal Engine • C++ • Music Composer
about.title: About Me
about.text: Game Development student specialized in programming, with a strong focus on C++ and Unreal Engine. I am particularly interested in gameplay systems, engine architecture, and performance optimization. I also work on music composition and sound design, as I believe audio plays a critical role in player experience. I enjoy understanding how systems work at a deep level, both technically and creatively. I love exploring all the possible ways to implement a function in order to determine the best option.
firstYear.title: First Year Projects
firstYear.sywar.desc: A turn‑based combat system featuring clickable areas to choose various actions. Built in C++ with SFML over the course of one week.
firstYear.zaun.desc: Shoot’em up featuring a wave system that spawns enemies in predefined patterns, ending with a final boss fight inspired by Arcane – League of Legends. Developed in C++ using SFML over a two‑week period.
firstYear.zeldo.desc: Collaborative three‑person project centered on developing player mechanics and a map‑generation system driven by .txt file parsing. Completed in two weeks.
firstYear.detective.desc: Individual project developed on a custom engine by Sylvain Seccia (Seccia.dev). Due to the absence of dedicated artists, the environment visuals were produced using AI‑generated assets.
firstYear.kathos.desc: Large‑scale team project where I acted as Lead Tech, coordinating 4 programmers, 2 artists, and 2 business students. Built in C++ with SFML within a three‑week timeframe.
secondYear.title: Second Year Projects
secondYear.mathlib.desc: A custom mathematics library written in C++ and completed within two weeks.
secondYear.pink.desc: Runner project designed to explore player physics and the 3Cs (Character, Camera, Control). Built in C++ with SFML within a two‑week timeframe.
secondYear.blender.desc: Introduction to artistic vocabulary and foundational 3D concepts using Blender, aimed at improving collaboration with artists. Completed in two weeks.
secondYear.arena.desc: A large‑scale collaborative project bringing together G‑Art and G‑Tech students, combining artistic and programming expertise. Developed using Unreal Engine 5.6 within a three‑week timeframe.
secondYear.multi.desc: Discovery and practical implementation of multiplayer systems in Unreal Engine 5.6, focusing on replication. Completed within two weeks.
secondYear.engine.desc: Custom Game Engine real time. Released in C++ in 4 weeks.
secondYear.intern.desc: Large‑scale Metaverse project, where I contributed to the creation and customization of vehicles in Earniverse, including boats, hoverboards, and horses.
